title: The man that was drowned.
html_source:
This is an interesting parallel to a similar Modernist work, T.S Eliot’s “The Waste Land” with the figure of the drowned Phoenician in Part 4, a sort of archetype derived from the Osiris and Fisher King myth.

Joyce may be trying to draw a parallel between Stephen (who is hinted to have lost his procreative powers running amuck with whores) and The Fisher King, who through union with the Questing Knight (possibly Leopold Bloom) is made whole. This line also relates to the marine imagery of the chapter with the “snot-green” sea.
